note: Original draft content written from general knowledge, unreviewed. Nothing was copied from a course, book, phrasebook or website. Pointing, transliteration (capitals mark the stressed syllable), register labels and gender forms have NOT been checked by a native speaker. No audio exists for any item. Nothing here was tested with learners.

scenarios.title: Order a milky coffee
scenarios.situation: You are at a counter in a cafe. The server is waiting for your order.

options.en: A hafuch, please?
options.explain: Short, polite, no gender to choose.

options.he: אֲנִי רוֹצֶה לְהַזְמִין קָפֶה הָפוּךְ, בְּבַקָּשָׁה
options.translit: ani roTSE lehazMIN kaFE haFUCH, bevakaSHA
options.en: I want to order a coffee hafuch, please.

m.he: אֲנִי רוֹצֶה לְהַזְמִין קָפֶה הָפוּךְ, בְּבַקָּשָׁה
m.translit: ani roTSE lehazMIN kaFE haFUCH, bevakaSHA

f.he: אֲנִי רוֹצָה לְהַזְמִין קָפֶה הָפוּךְ, בְּבַקָּשָׁה
f.translit: ani roTSA lehazMIN kaFE haFUCH, bevakaSHA

options.en: Hafuch, come on, quickly.
options.explain: Yalla plus 'quickly' sounds pushy to a stranger who is serving you.

scenarios.title: Ask for the bill
scenarios.situation: You have finished your meal and the waiter walks by.

options.en: Everything's great. Bill, please?
options.explain: Answers the question, then asks briefly.

options.he: הַאִם אֶפְשָׁר לְקַבֵּל אֶת הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן לְשֻׁלְחָנֵנוּ?
options.translit: ha'IM efSHAR lekaBEL et hacheshBON leshulchaNEnu?
options.en: May we receive the bill for our table?
Come on, the bill! Already!
options.explain: Impatient. Nu and kvar with a stranger can sound rude.

scenarios.title: Ask for a better price
scenarios.situation: A vendor says 'twenty shekels a kilo'. You would like a lower price.

options.en: Give me a price?
options.explain: A light request that is commonly heard in markets (to a male vendor).

options.he: הַאִם תִּהְיֶה מוּכָן לְהוֹרִיד אֶת הַמְּחִיר?
options.translit: ha'IM tihYE muCHAN lehoRID et hamechIR?
options.en: Would you be prepared to lower the price?
options.explain: Grammatical but much too formal for a stall.

options.he: זֶה גְּנֵבָה! אֲנִי לֹא מְשַׁלֵּם כָּל כָּךְ הַרְבֵּה!
options.translit: ze gneVA! ani lo meshaLEM kol KACH harBE!
options.en: That's robbery! I won't pay so much!
options.explain: Accusing the seller will not help.

m.he: זֶה גְּנֵבָה! אֲנִי לֹא מְשַׁלֵּם כָּל כָּךְ הַרְבֵּה!
m.translit: ze gneVA! ani lo meshaLEM kol KACH harBE!

f.he: זֶה גְּנֵבָה! אֲנִי לֹא מְשַׁלֶּמֶת כָּל כָּךְ הַרְבֵּה!
f.translit: ze gneVA! ani lo meshaLEmet kol KACH harBE!

scenarios.title: Ask for something for a headache
scenarios.situation: The pharmacist (a man) asks how he can help.

options.he: כּוֹאֵב לִי הָרֹאשׁ. יֵשׁ מַשֶּׁהוּ לָזֶה?
options.translit: ko'EV li haROSH. YESH maSHEhu laZE?
options.en: My head hurts. Is there something for it?

options.he: אֲנִי סוֹבֵל מִכְּאֵב רֹאשׁ. אֶפְשָׁר תְּרוּפָה?
options.translit: ani soVEL mike'EV rosh. efSHAR tru'FA?
options.en: I suffer from a headache. Is a medicine possible?
options.explain: Heavy: 'I suffer' sounds like a medical report.

m.he: אֲנִי סוֹבֵל מִכְּאֵב רֹאשׁ. אֶפְשָׁר תְּרוּפָה?
m.translit: ani soVEL mike'EV rosh. efSHAR tru'FA?

f.he: אֲנִי סוֹבֶלֶת מִכְּאֵב רֹאשׁ. אֶפְשָׁר תְּרוּפָה?
f.translit: ani soVElet mike'EV rosh. efSHAR tru'FA?

options.he: אָחִי, הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁלִּי בָּלָגָן, תֵּן מַשֶּׁהוּ
options.translit: aCHI, haROSH sheLI balaGAN, TEN maSHEhu
options.en: Mate, my head is a mess, give me something.
options.explain: Slang for a professional, and balagan means 'mess', not pain.

scenarios.title: Check the bus
scenarios.situation: You are at a stop. The bus arrives and the driver opens the door.

options.en: Does this go to the centre?
Does this bus travel to the centre?
Driver, the centre, yes or no?
options.explain: Curt, and 'driver' as a form of address sounds blunt.

scenarios.title: Stop the taxi
scenarios.situation: You are near your hotel and want the taxi to stop.

options.en: Stop here, please.

options.he: הַאִם תִּהְיֶה מוּכָן לַעֲצֹר בְּמָקוֹם זֶה?
options.translit: ha'IM tihYE muCHAN la'aTSOR bemaKOM ze?
options.en: Would you be prepared to stop at this place?
Enough, enough, stop already!
options.explain: Sounds panicky or annoyed for a simple request.

scenarios.title: Buy a train ticket
scenarios.situation: You are at a ticket window for a train to Haifa.

options.en: Return to Haifa, please.

options.he: אֲנִי רוֹצֶה לִרְכֹּשׁ כַּרְטִיס הָלוֹךְ וָשׁוֹב לְחֵיפָה
options.translit: ani roTSE lirKOSH karTIS haLOCH vaSHOV lecheiFA
options.en: I want to purchase a return ticket to Haifa.

m.he: אֲנִי רוֹצֶה לִרְכֹּשׁ כַּרְטִיס הָלוֹךְ וָשׁוֹב לְחֵיפָה
m.translit: ani roTSE lirKOSH karTIS haLOCH vaSHOV lecheiFA

f.he: אֲנִי רוֹצָה לִרְכֹּשׁ כַּרְטִיס הָלוֹךְ וָשׁוֹב לְחֵיפָה
f.translit: ani roTSA lirKOSH karTIS haLOCH vaSHOV lecheiFA

options.en: Hi, Haifa, return, come on.
options.explain: Too slangy and pushy for a window.

scenarios.title: Ask an older stranger the way
scenarios.situation: You want the post office and see an older man on the street.

options.en: Excuse me, where is the post office?

options.he: סְלִיחָה אֲדוֹנִי, הַאִם תּוּכַל לוֹמַר לִי הֵיכָן נִמְצָא סְנִיף הַדֹּאַר?
options.translit: sliCHA adoNI, ha'IM tuCHAL lo'MAR li hei'CHAN nimTSA snif haDO'ar?
options.en: Excuse me sir, could you tell me where the post office branch is located?
options.explain: Heichan and the long frame are formal.

options.en: Hey mate, where's the post office?
options.explain: Slang for an older stranger. Save achi for peers.

scenarios.title: Thank a stranger
scenarios.situation: A man you do not know holds the door for you.

options.en: Thanks!

options.he: אֲנִי מוֹדֶה לְךָ מְאוֹד עַל כָּךְ
options.translit: ani moDE lecha me'OD al KACH
options.en: I thank you very much for that.
options.explain: Much too grand for a held door.

m.he: אֲנִי מוֹדֶה לְךָ מְאוֹד עַל כָּךְ
m.translit: ani moDE lecha me'OD al KACH

f.he: אֲנִי מוֹדָה לְךָ מְאוֹד עַל כָּךְ
f.translit: ani moDA lecha me'OD al KACH

options.en: My pleasure!
options.explain: That is a reply to thanks, not a way to give it.

scenarios.note: The wrong option is wrong in function.

scenarios.title: Say sorry for being late
scenarios.situation: You meet a friend and you are ten minutes late.

options.en: Sorry I'm late!
I regret the delay very much.
Not my fault, there was traffic.

scenarios.note: The wrong option is wrong in tone, not grammar.
scenarios.confidenceReason: The wrong option is wrong in tone, not grammar.

scenarios.title: Answer a call
scenarios.situation: Your phone rings from an unknown number.

options.en: Hello?
Hello, who is speaking, if possible?
Come on, who is this?

scenarios.title: Text that you are on the way
scenarios.situation: A friend writes: 'How much longer?' You are on the way.

options.en: On the way, five more minutes.

options.he: אֲנִי נִמְצָא בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְאַגִּיעַ בְּעוֹד כַּחֲמֵשׁ דַּקּוֹת
options.translit: ani nimTSA baDErech ve'agIa be'OD kachaMESH daKOT
options.en: I am on the way and will arrive in about five minutes.
options.explain: Correct but far too formal for a chat.

m.he: אֲנִי נִמְצָא בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְאַגִּיעַ בְּעוֹד כַּחֲמֵשׁ דַּקּוֹת
m.translit: ani nimTSA baDErech ve'agIa be'OD kachaMESH daKOT

f.he: אֲנִי נִמְצֵאת בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְאַגִּיעַ בְּעוֹד כַּחֲמֵשׁ דַּקּוֹת
f.translit: ani nimTSEt baDErech ve'agIa be'OD kachaMESH daKOT

options.en: Behold, I'm on the way.
options.explain: Hineni is a biblical word; it sounds like a joke here.

scenarios.title: Meet a friend's father
scenarios.situation: You are introduced to your friend's father at his home.

options.en: Very nice to meet you.

options.he: אֲנִי שָׂמֵחַ לְהִתְוַדַּע אֵלֶיךָ בְּאֹפֶן אִישִׁי
options.translit: ani saMEaCH lehitvaDA eLEcha be'OfEN ishi
options.en: I am pleased to make your personal acquaintance.

m.he: אֲנִי שָׂמֵחַ לְהִתְוַדַּע אֵלֶיךָ בְּאֹפֶן אִישִׁי
m.translit: ani saMEaCH lehitvaDA eLEcha be'OfEN ishi

f.he: אֲנִי שְׂמֵחָה לְהִתְוַדַּע אֵלֶיךָ בְּאֹפֶן אִישִׁי
f.translit: ani semeCHA lehitvaDA eLEcha be'OfEN ishi

options.en: What's up, mate?
options.explain: Too casual for meeting a friend's father.

scenarios.title: Ask someone to slow down
scenarios.situation: Someone answers you very quickly and you did not follow.

options.en: Sorry, could you go slower?

options.he: הַאִם יִתָּכֵן לַחֲזֹר עַל הַדְּבָרִים לְאַט יוֹתֵר?
options.translit: ha'IM yitaKEN lachaZOR al hadvaRIM le'AT yoTER?
options.en: Would it be possible to repeat the matter more slowly?

options.he: מָה? מָה? אֲנִי לֹא מֵבִין כְּלוּם!
options.translit: MA? MA? ani lo meVIN kluM!
options.en: What? What? I understand nothing!

m.he: מָה? מָה? אֲנִי לֹא מֵבִין כְּלוּם!
m.translit: MA? MA? ani lo meVIN kluM!

f.he: מָה? מָה? אֲנִי לֹא מְבִינָה כְּלוּם!
f.translit: MA? MA? ani lo mevinA kluM!

scenarios.title: Agree to an appointment time
scenarios.situation: A clerk asks: 'Is ten o'clock okay for the appointment?'

options.en: Yes, ten is fine.
I agree to the proposed date.
Cool mate.

scenarios.title: Say goodbye on Friday
scenarios.situation: It is Friday afternoon and you leave a shop.

options.en: Shabbat shalom!
I wish you a peaceful Sabbath.
Good week!
options.explain: Said once Shabbat has ended, not on Friday.

scenarios.note: The wrong option is wrong in timing.
